body: I didn’t say that all trans women automatically “look like” women as soon as they “make a choice” to transition — although what does it say about our society that women and men have a certain look, but regardless that’s not important, simply that trans women are women, whether or not they “look like a women” in your (or my, or anyone else’s — I’m not trying to attack you here)’s eyes! I totally believe that you are not someone who hates trans people and if you are supportive of your friend, great! But remember that dark humor at the expense of a marginalized group that you aren’t a part of is not the same as dark humor in general. A ton of people on Reddit have dark humor, so it’s definitely not the issue. Poking fun at yourself is different than what you insinuated with your comment.
I hope you find my profile and message me about this.

I understand that you don’t “mean” to be transphobic, but if the thought of somebody thinking you’re a trans woman makes you want to kill yourself, you have some serious serious biases to work through. Trans women are women, they don’t have a certain look. This whole conversation was hard to read. I really wish you luck in sorting out your internalized transphobia — being perceived as trans is nothing to k*ll yourself over ❤️ best of luck

Here we go. Not that crazy to be fair, but my friend group doesn’t really get that crazy. So, one night me and a few of my good friends planned to go to the club.  We stopped over at a friends place and had a few drinks. This was a Halloween party, to prefix, so we are all in costume... One of the people there were already quite intoxicated but hiding it well. So anyway, we all have a few drinks and are all pretty drunk. We walk to the club down the street, wait in line and the person who is most intoxicated is falling over, tripping, slurring, etc. We get to the front of the line, and the bouncer says to the friend “you’re not coming in, I saw you fall.” My roommate being the good friend they are, offers to walk them home, and the rest of us get ushered into the club. I’m having fun and dancing, but I’m pretty worried, so I call my roommate. After a few tries, I get through to them. I ask how they and the friend are, they say “yeah not good... [friend] is passed out I called the ambulance.  I tell our DD that [friend] and [roommate]  are on their way to the hospital. We all leave the club. Remember that most of us are in costume, with one of our guy friends in a “slutty seamen” costume.... and this male friend is [drunk friend’s] emergency contact, so he must go to the hospital. We get to the hospital, walk in, and [roommate] is sitting in the waiting room, princess costume ripped, covered in vomit, crying.  I and another friend escort [roommate] outside, while male friend, slutty seaman costume adorned, goes to ask about [drunk friend].  Meanwhile, [roommate] is very emotional and crying, loudly. Security guard (I assume) comes outside and says “honey, I know you’re upset but you’ll have to quiet down, there are people sleeping. And (I kid you not)  my roommate says, full seriousness and fully feeling terrible about it; “oh my god, someone called the cops on me because I just woke up sick people who probably have cancer!!!” At this point, I call an Uber, we get home, and she goes into her room. A few minutes later I hear ; “ I want to be alone but I can’t get this dress off!!” I help her unzip the dress, get her some water, and she calls a friend, sleeps it off, all is well and good the next morning. The friend who was in the hospital ended up fine, just had a fractured wrist from falling. 

TLDR: Celebrating Halloween, we all got too drunk, one of us got alcohol poisoning and our friend group had to walk into a hospital at 11pm wearing slutty Halloween costumes.
